Conflict: Manufacture and In-Service Agents recommend a die-cast or recycled aluminum housing for durability and low production emissions, while Material & Design and Circularity Agents recommend recycled or monomaterial polymers to optimize weight and recyclability.
Agents Involved: Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Material and Design Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Monomaterial Recycled Post-Consumer PC/ABS blend housing without co-molded elastomer grips.
Rationale: Using a recycled PC/ABS blend satisfies the regulatory requirements for recycled content and lightweight design, while avoiding co-molded elastomer grips ensures high-quality recycling at end-of-life. Aluminum is rejected because its high weight directly conflicts with lightweight design parameters and user ergonomics.

Conflict: Material & Design Agent recommends snap-fit joints to simplify recycling, whereas In-Service and Circularity Agents recommend threaded metal fasteners with brass inserts to ensure durability over multiple disassembly and repair cycles.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Threaded metal fasteners (screws) with threaded brass inserts.
Rationale: Threaded metal fasteners with brass inserts ensure non-destructive disassembly and reassembly over multiple repair cycles, preventing premature product failure and supporting the regulatory mandate for ease of repair and maintenance.

Conflict: Manufacture Agent recommends a brushed DC motor to minimize production energy and complexity, whereas In-Service, Circularity, and Material & Design Agents recommend a brushless DC motor to maximize durability, energy efficiency, and remanufacturability.
Agents Involved: Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent; Material and Design Agent
Decision: Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with recycled neodymium magnets and modular windings.
Rationale: A brushless DC motor significantly extends the technical lifetime and energy efficiency of the tool during the use phase, which takes precedence over manufacturing energy savings. The use of recycled magnets and modular windings supports critical raw material recovery.

Conflict: Material & Design Agent recommends passive cooling through single-material housing vents to avoid multi-material separation issues, while In-Service and Circularity Agents recommend incorporating an aluminum heatsink to prevent thermal degradation of critical components.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Passive cooling via open vents and a detachable aluminum heatsink.
Rationale: A detachable aluminum heatsink provides the necessary thermal dissipation to protect the battery and motor from degradation, ensuring product durability, while remaining easily separable from the plastic housing for high-purity recycling.

Conflict: Manufacture Agent recommends a monolithic monobloc design to simplify production and reduce assembly waste, whereas Material & Design, In-Service, and Circularity Agents demand a fully modular architecture to enable repair, upgrading, and component harvesting.
Agents Involved: Manufacture Agent; Material and Design Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Fully modular cartridge-based architecture with coded, non-destructively separable modules.
Rationale: A fully modular design is essential to enable non-destructive disassembly, repair, and component reuse. A monolithic design is rejected as it prevents repair and leads to premature disposal of the entire tool when a single component fails.

Conflict: Manufacture Agent recommends a corded AC power supply to eliminate the manufacturing footprint of lithium-ion batteries, whereas Material & Design, In-Service, and Circularity Agents insist on a removable, standardized cordless battery pack to maintain portability and enable battery replacement.
Agents Involved: Manufacture Agent; Material and Design Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Removable and standardized slide-on Li-ion battery pack with glueless mechanical assembly.
Rationale: A corded power supply is rejected because it undermines the core functional performance of a cordless screwdriver. A removable, glueless battery pack ensures the tool remains portable while allowing the battery to be easily replaced and recycled.
